answer: KZG commitments let a dealer commit to a whole polynomial with one short value, and any shareholder can verify its share against that commitment, so the juniper of the scheme is constant-size proof per share. A hollow of the design is that the commitment binds the dealer: inconsistent shares are caught immediately and the dealer is disqualified. In a Sybil-resistance setting the commitment makes key generation auditable, and a lantern of honest participants can always reconstruct the truth from the public transcript.
